title: pH Meter

references.label: General microbiology laboratory manuals (ASM curriculum resources)
Biosafety in Microbiological and Biomedical Laboratories (BMBL)

purpose: Measures the hydrogen ion activity (pH) of a solution electrochemically, used for checking/adjusting media and reagent pH.
operatingPrinciple: A glass electrode develops a voltage proportional to the difference in hydrogen ion concentration between the sample and a reference, which the meter converts to a pH reading.
basicOperation: Calibrate using at least two standard buffer solutions bracketing the expected sample pH before each use session.
Rinse the electrode with distilled water between the buffer and the sample, and between different samples.
Allow the reading to stabilize before recording.
importantSettings: Calibration buffer selection, chosen to bracket the expected sample pH range.
calibration: Must be calibrated with fresh standard buffers at the start of each use session (or per facility SOP) — a meter's calibration drifts over time and with temperature.
maintenance: Store the electrode per manufacturer instructions (commonly in a storage solution, not dry) to prevent the glass membrane from drying out.
Replace probes that no longer calibrate reliably.

commonErrors.cause: Electrode not properly calibrated, dried-out membrane, or air bubble at the tip
commonErrors.fix: Recalibrate with fresh buffers and inspect/recondition the electrode per manufacturer instructions

safety: Handle buffer/calibration solutions per their safety data sheets.
